rebuttal_or_critique: I remain firmly of the view that the 'withdrawal of accommodation' stance is no longer appropriate. With core inflation at 4.10%, the real policy rate is already significantly positive and restrictive. The persistence of food inflation at 8.70% is a supply-side issue that cannot be solved by further monetary tightening, which only serves to threaten the 6.50% GVA growth momentum. Maintaining a stance that implies further tightening is unnecessary and risks an over-correction. I must dissent from the majority on the stance, as a neutral stance is the only one consistent with the current macroeconomic data.
